scope: These credits describe the ORCHID project and its examples. Cite the papers and software used in your analysis, together with the ORCHID release and original source of each observation. The list does not imply that every dataset was generated with every package. Preserve the versions and commit hashes recorded by each example; a repository link is not a reproducibility pin. Materials Project and OQMD energies retain separate references.

credits.name: pycalphad
papers: R. Otis and Z.-K. Liu (2017), pycalphad: CALPHAD-based Computational Thermodynamics in Python

credits.name: ESPEI
credits.role: Thermodynamic parameter fitting and uncertainty quantification
papers: B. Bocklund et al. (2019), ESPEI for efficient thermodynamic database development, modification, and uncertainty quantification: application to Cu–Mg

credits.name: PhaseForge
credits.role: MLIP-informed CALPHAD construction in the examples
papers: S. Zhu, D. Sarıtürk, and R. Arróyave (2025), Machine learning potentials for alloys: a detailed workflow to predict phase diagrams and benchmark accuracy

credits.name: PhaseForge+
credits.role: Construction and experimental tuning of CALPHAD models in the examples; repository name PhaseForgePlus
papers: C. Kunselman, S. Zhu, D. Sarıtürk, and R. Arróyave (2025), Construction and Tuning of CALPHAD Models Using Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials and Experimental Data: A Case Study of the Pt–W System

credits.name: MaterialsFramework
credits.role: Uniform interface to machine-learning interatomic potentials (single-point energies, relaxations, molecular dynamics) used by PhaseForge and directly in the ORCHID examples and MLIP benchmarks

credits.name: Materials Project
credits.role: DFT structures and energies; repository link is the API client, not the database itself
papers: A. Jain et al. (2013), Commentary: The Materials Project: A materials genome approach to accelerating materials innovation

credits.name: OQMD
credits.role: DFT structures and energies; qmpy is the supporting software
papers: J. E. Saal et al. (2013), Materials Design and Discovery with High-Throughput Density Functional Theory: The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD)
S. Kirklin et al. (2015), The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD): assessing the accuracy of DFT formation energies
